content: The test image shows a split corn stalk with orange-brown pith discoloration and numerous small black dots (pycnidia/perithecia) embedded throughout the tissue. Let me compare with candidate reference images.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Split corn stalk showing internal pith tissue
- Orange-brown/tan discoloration of pith
- Numerous small, discrete black dots (pycnidia/fruiting bodies) scattered uniformly throughout the pith tissue
- Fibrous texture of the degraded pith
- Top of image shows corn ear base (kernels visible)

**Comparison with references:**
- **Diplodia stalk rot**: The reference shows external stalk views; Diplodia characteristically produces small black pycnidia in the disintegrating orange-brown pith — matches the test image very well
- **Anthracnose stalk rot**: Shows shredded/stringy pith with black external lesions; the internal pattern differs
- **Charcoal stalk rot**: Shows gray-silver pith with black sclerotia (larger, more diffuse); the test image has a more orange-brown tone with smaller, discrete pycnidia
- **Physoderma stalk rot**: Shows mostly brown external lesions at the stalk base, not the internal pycnidial pattern seen here

The orange-tan pith with uniformly scattered small black pycnidia is the hallmark presentation of **Diplodia stalk rot** (*Stenocarpella maydis*).
